Evan / Northridge security team — hi, Markus from Redwood Security (InfoSec / Compliance). Thanks for the clear asks. Summary below; full responses are attached (SIG_Response_v2.xlsx) and a SOC 2 scope summary (SOC2_Type2_summary_2025.pdf).

High-level:
- SOC 2: Our Type II report (2025) covers Redwood's Production inference and control plane services. It excludes customer-managed on-prem packages (those are covered under separate attestations when deployed).
- KMS & keying: We use a layered approach: platform-managed keys in AWS KMS for platform-level secrets and per-tenant envelope encryption for customer data. Customer-managed keys (CMKs) are available in Redwood Private and Dedicated offerings; hosted customers can request a Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) flow under an enterprise agreement.
- Key rotation: Automated rotation at both envelope and platform key levels; rotation policies retained in our key-management runbook.
- Inference logs: Default: pseudonymized request IDs and metadata are stored; raw inputs are not retained beyond configured retention windows unless explicitly enabled by the customer. For customers requiring CMKs for logs, we offer an option in Dedicated/Private modes.
- SIG: Attached spreadsheet contains row-by-row answers to the CAIQ sections you flagged and links to the underlying evidence. For any "partial" answers we included an explanation and a Jira ticket (JIRA-SEC-4127) with remediation timelines.

Attachments (stubs): SIG_Response_v2.xlsx (55 tabs — crypto-focused), SOC2_Type2_summary_2025.pdf

If you need the full SOC 2 report executed under NDA, we can route that via our security portal — let me know and I'll open an access request.

Quote of your earlier point:
> "particularly interested in KMS, key rotation, and whether you use customer-managed keys for inference logs"

Answer: yes for Dedicated/Private (BYOK supported), no for default hosted unless on an enterprise agreement with BYOK enabled.

I'll be available for a 30-minute deep dive Tues/Wednesday (PST) to walk through the SIG rows.

Regards,
Markus Klein
